findings.title: Uncapped daily liquidated damages based on Total Contract Value
findings.deviation: The contract imposes uncapped liquidated damages of 2% of the Total Contract Value per day, allows actual damages in addition to LDs, and has no exclusion for client-caused delay. AtliQ's standard is 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone fee, as the sole remedy, with an exclusion for client-caused delay.
findings.impact: AtliQ could face astronomical, uncapped daily penalties calculated on the entire contract value even for minor delays, on top of being liable for actual damages.
findings.quote: if Contractor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Contractor shall pay Client, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Contract Value for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.
findings.counterPosition: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone fee; no LDs where the delay is caused by the client; LDs are the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.

findings.title: One-sided limitation of liability and unlimited Contractor liability
findings.deviation: The contract caps the Client's liability but explicitly states that Contractor has unlimited liability for all losses, including indemnification, BAA breaches, and data security incidents. AtliQ's standard requires a mutual cap of 1x fees paid/payable in the prior 12 months, with data protection capped under a separate super-cap.
findings.impact: AtliQ would face unlimited financial liability for any breach or data incident, while the Client's exposure remains strictly capped.
findings.quote: NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE CONTRACTOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING CONTRACTOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, BREACH OF THE BAA, OR ANY DATA SECURITY INCIDENT.
findings.counterPosition: Mutual cap of 1× fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim; carve-outs limited to fraud, wilful misconduct and breach of confidentiality; data-protection liability under a separate super-cap (e.g. 2× fees).

findings.title: Broad unilateral indemnity covering Client's own negligence
findings.deviation: AtliQ is required to indemnify Client for any losses relating to the Services or deliverables regardless of whether they are caused in part by the Client's own negligence, while the Client's indemnity is limited only to gross negligence or willful misconduct. AtliQ's standard is a mutual indemnity for third-party claims caused by each party's own breach or negligence, with no coverage for the other party's negligence.
findings.impact: AtliQ could be forced to pay for losses and legal defenses even when the Client's own negligence contributed to the claim.
findings.quote: regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any Client Indemnitee.
findings.counterPosition: Each party indemnifies the other for third-party claims caused by its own breach or negligence; no indemnity for losses caused by the indemnified party's own negligence; indemnities subject to the liability cap (IP infringement excepted).

findings.title: IP vesting from creation and assignment of pre-existing materials
findings.deviation: Deliverables are designated as works made for hire vesting from creation prior to payment, and the contract purports to assign Pre-Existing Materials incorporated into deliverables. AtliQ's standard requires that ownership vests only upon payment, and that background IP/pre-existing materials are retained by AtliQ with a license granted to the Client.
findings.impact: AtliQ loses its proprietary background IP and tools incorporated into deliverables, and ownership of deliverables transfers before AtliQ is paid.
findings.quote: All Deliverables shall be deemed "works made for hire" as defined in the U.S. Copyright Act, 17 U.S.C. § 101, and shall be the sole and exclusive property of Client from creation.
findings.counterPosition: Client owns deliverables created specifically for it upon payment; AtliQ retains background IP and grants a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use it as part of the deliverables.

findings.title: Short notice and no payment for WIP upon convenience termination
findings.deviation: The Client may terminate for convenience on 7 days' notice, and AtliQ is only entitled to payment for accepted deliverables, completely excluding work in progress. AtliQ's standard requires a reasonable notice period (at least 30 days) and full payment for all work performed up to termination, including work in progress.
findings.impact: AtliQ could have its contract terminated with almost no warning and be left unpaid for substantial uncompleted or unaccepted work in progress.
findings.quote: upon seven (7) days' written notice to Contractor. Upon such termination, Client's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by Client prior to the effective date of termination; Client shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables, demobilization costs or anticipated profits.
findings.counterPosition: Payment for all services performed up to termination, including work in progress and committed costs; mutual notice period of at least 30 days.

findings.title: Insurance limits exceed AtliQ's actual coverage
findings.deviation: The contract requires AtliQ to maintain $5,000,000 in cyber liability insurance, whereas AtliQ's standard coverage is $1,000,000.
findings.impact: AtliQ would be in breach of contract from day one unless it negotiates a lower limit or purchases additional, expensive insurance coverage.
findings.counterPosition: Align required limits with current cover (cyber liability limit of $1,000,000), or agree a timeline and cost to increase cover before signature.

findings.title: Broad cross-agreement set-off right for Client
findings.deviation: The contract allows the Client to set off any amounts owed by AtliQ under this or any other agreement. AtliQ's standard is to limit set-off to undisputed amounts arising strictly under the same agreement.
findings.impact: The Client could withhold payments due under this contract to settle unrelated, disputed claims under other contracts, disrupting AtliQ's cash flow.
findings.quote: Client may set off against any amount owed to Contractor any amount owed by Contractor to Client under this Agreement or any other agreement.
findings.counterPosition: set-off limited to undisputed amounts under this agreement.

fine.note: Confidentiality obligations are mutual in substance and standard.
The BAA requirements and offshore restrictions are aligned with standard data protection practices.
The agreement does not contain any restrictive covenants or non-competes.
The acceptance process provides a clear 30-day testing window.
Warranties are standard for professional services and intellectual property non-infringement.
